note: RETROSPECTIVE 2026-09-04 (lane R13; findings A12#0/#1/#2/#8, A9#5): every line was re-diagnosed against the committed baselines and re-measured with the shipping metric stack (padToCanvas → pixelmatch 0.02/includeAA:false → ssim.js fast → CIEDE2000 stride 4 → classifyDivergence, exactly compare-screenshots.mjs diffPair); `observed` is that re-measurement, `observedAt` its date, `observedFrom` its provenance. The seed's 'corner AA' story was WRONG for 14 lines: the visible divergence is a CLIP asymmetry (iOS clips in-flow content to the rounded shape; both natives clip under background-image layers; Android drops descendant ink under blur), and the seed's 'edgeSSIM 1.00' was the then-broken all-ones metric. `owner` is a lane/mechanism handle (platform-category-mechanism), never a person. Lines whose fix is in flight are marked EXPECTED STALE: exit 5 at the next gate names them and the only action is DELETE. Expiry decisions are written into each reason. ORIGINAL SEED NOTE FOLLOWS. Known cross-platform divergences on fixtures/visual-test.json, seeded from a live three-platform run (327 pairs, 23 failing at SSIM<0.95 || dpx>2%). A LEDGER, not a tolerance: each line names one divergence, why it is believed benign or why it is a bug, who owns it, and when it must be re-reviewed. Deleting a line is how a fix gets recorded. READ THIS: 6 of these entries are REAL SIZE BUGS surfaced for the first time by the magenta pad sentinel - before that fix a short render was padded with the capture background and scored a perfect diff. They carry a short expiry because they need fixing, not excusing. Of the remainder, almost all fail on SSIM alone with dpx well under the 2% budget and deltaE95 = 0.00 - the colours are exact and SSIM is scoring curve/transform anti-aliasing. That is evidence about the METRIC, not the runtimes, and most of those lines should evaporate when the gate moves off SSIM. ALSO measured on composition-test.json (2026-08-26): pixelmatch at threshold 0.25 reported pixelMismatchedPct 0.00 for 037_Nested_OpacityGroup while 36.63% of pixels differ by up to 80 per channel. Its YIQ budget is 0.25*35215 = 8803.8, and a PURE LIGHTNESS shift must exceed 132/255 to be counted — so black (0,0,0) vs mid-grey (130,130,130) is reported as identical. The 2% pixel gate therefore cannot fire on any uniform lightness error smaller than half the dynamic range. Only SSIM (0.9355) and deltaE95 (20.94) caught this row. KEYS ARE INDEX-FREE: entries store the component NAME without the capture's {NNN}_ prefix, because that prefix is a position in the flattened capture list and renumbers whenever the corpus changes.

expectations.reason: NOT a runtime gap — CORRECTED 2026-08-28. backdrop-filter IS implemented on both natives (docs/STATUS.md wave 26: a two-pass controlled-canvas model, validated on iOS against browser refs at 0.966 / 0.978 / 0.999, edge model later corrected against Chrome). What the control measured is a CAPTURE-MODE gate, not a missing applier: the two-pass path arms only on the COMPOSED capture path and is deliberately disarmed on the per-component path this fixture runs through. Android: `wantsBackdropPass = composedMode && documentDeclaresBackdropFilter(composed)` (ScreenshotCaptureScreen.kt:309). iOS: ScreenshotCaptureView states it outright — 'Lane BF-I deliberately does NOT two-pass here... the WPT paths below, where a backdrop element actually has neighbours, are where the two-pass runs.' expectations.reason: iOS CLIP ASYMMETRY, not corner AA (re-diagnosed 2026-09-04, retro A12#0; the seed's 'edgeSSIM 1.00' was the then-broken all-ones metric). runtimes/swiftui/Sources/StyleConverterRuntime/StyleEngine/borders/radius/BorderRadiusApplier.swift applied `.clipShape(BorderRadiusShape)` UNCONDITIONALLY, so iOS clips in-flow content — here the block-font label — to the rounded box while Android and web paint it past the box edge. css-backgrounds-3 §4.3 (Corner Clipping) bounds the element's OWN background and border painting at the curve; descendants are clipped only when overflow is not visible (css-overflow-3 §3.1, the clip rounded per §3.1.2). Committed baselines, ink right of x=80 (pixels more than 40/255 from the ground in any channel): iOS 0 px vs Android 204 / web 204; dE95 0.00 because every surviving pixel is the right colour, and the Android-web pair of this component PASSES — rasteriser AA would separate Android from web too. Android's twin was fixed wave 41 T5 (BorderRadiusApplier.kt selfPaintsWithoutClip). FIX IN FLIGHT: retro R4 gates the iOS clip behind clipsDescendants (self-paint + .contentShape while overflow is visible). EXPECTED STALE at the next visual-test gate: exit 5 names this line — the action is DELETE, never re-add.

expectations.reason: REAL BUG (Android), and narrower than first recorded — it is the PLACEHOLDER FLOOR, not the box model. Android renders this component 2x(border-width) shorter than iOS/web: Button_Outline and Edge_DeepNesting (border 2px) are 4px short, Input_Field (border 1px) is 2px short, and Button_Primary / Border_Solid / Border_Dashed / Border_Mixed — borders without a floor-driven height — are all exact. Two measurements narrow it: (a) with real text pinned (fixtures/visual-test-controls.json) removing the border changes the Android box by EXACTLY 2x its width (Input_Field 54->52 at 1px, Edge_DeepNesting 52->48 at 2px), so the border box is computed correctly when content determines the size; (b) Input_Field's EXPLICIT width:200px is exact on all three while only its unconstrained, floor-driven height is short. So the defect is in StyleApplier.placeholderFloorMinSize / borderBoxFloorMins, which converts web's border-box minHeight:30px into a Compose content-box defaultMinSize by subtracting padding + band. That floor exists ONLY because visual-test.json has no text; it is harness scaffolding matching web's scaffolding, not product behaviour. Note the area's history: the same arithmetic caused +2px regressions in wave-1 (Input_Field/Glass_Effect) and wave-4 (every Decorated row), so change it with a measured before/after, not by reasoning. RE-REVIEWED 2026-09-04 (retro R13, A12#8): still present in the committed baselines (Android 390x58 / 390x60 vs 390x62 on iOS and web), re-measured dpx 7.457% / dE95 49.707; StyleApplier.placeholderFloorMinSize (StyleApplier.kt:867) and borderBoxFloorMins (:910) are untouched and no fix lane was staffed in the retrospective. Expiry deliberately LEFT at 2026-09-30 — a real bug's short expiry is the forcing function the seed intended; the wave-50 gate reporting it past-expiry is the correct outcome until a MEASURED fix lands. Do not extend; fix or accept.

expectations.reason: ANDROID DROPS DESCENDANT INK UNDER filter: blur(), not a Gaussian-quantisation band (re-diagnosed 2026-09-04, retro A12#2). Modifier.blur records the subtree into a RenderNode sized to the node bounds, so even with BlurredEdgeTreatment.Unbounded a descendant painting outside the element is cropped: the blurred label beyond the box is present on iOS and web and ABSENT on Android (committed baselines, pixels right of x=80 more than 8/255 from the ground: iOS 368 / Android 0 / web 391). The diff IS the missing label — dpx 2.34 / 2.43 with dE95 ≤ 0.83 — and the iOS-web pair PASSES. filter-effects-1 §6.1 (blur()) blurs the element's whole rendering and §8 (Filter Region) extends the effect past the border box; nothing clips descendants, and FilterApplier.kt's own KDoc says overflow ink must survive. FIX IN FLIGHT: retro R6 replaces Modifier.blur with an unbounded GraphicsLayer (BlurLayerNode). EXPECTED STALE at the next visual-test gate: exit 5 names this line — the action is DELETE (R6 carries the deletion patch).
